title: Label wrap: scope and entry points amended after measuring each diagram kind

v:
Amends decision `01M4R4WDZ` (labels wrap at Mermaid's wrapping width). That decision was written before
each diagram kind was measured; mermaid 11.17.2 in headless Chrome showed two of its rules too broad or
too narrow. Where the two disagree, this one governs.

## Changes

1. **Rule 6, scope — notes.** "Never wraps: … notes" is narrowed to **sequence-diagram notes**. A
   state-diagram note wraps at 175 (Mermaid: 200px `break-spaces`, 3 rows, note box 230×102). Class-diagram
   notes follow whatever Mermaid is measured to do (recorded when class wrapping lands).
2. **Rule 6, scope — state.** A state's quoted name and its description wrap at 175; a transition label at
   150; a composite state's title does not wrap (Mermaid draws it `nowrap`). An unbreakable id overflows
   (rule 4).
3. **Rule 8, entry points.** `wrapLabel(label, measureText, wrapWidth, spacing?)` takes the row spacing
   (`LineSpacing`) the label is laid out at. `wrapConnectorLabel(label, measureText)` pairs the 150px width,
   the 12px connector measurer and the 18px row spacing so connector callers cannot mismatch them; a
   node-size counterpart pairs 175 with 14px text.
4. **Row spacing (new).** A label's rows are one line apart, a line being the drawn font size × 24/16 (Mermaid's
   24px line at 16px), with the measurer's vertical padding added once around the rows. Sequence text
   follows Mermaid's SVG text instead: messages, notes and block conditions at 19/16, participants and box
   captions at 1.0.

Everything else in `01M4R4WDZ` stands.
